L1720: ## 5. Nonclinical Pharmacology/Toxicology
L1721: ## 5.1. Executive Summary
L1722: The proposed product is a bilayer oral tablet that consists of a fixed dose combination of sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid. Sulopenem etzadroxil (PF-03709270) is a prodrug that is rapidly cleaved upon intestinal absorption to generate its active metabolite, sulopenem (CP-70429) which is a penem antibacterial drug. Penem antibacterial drugs are known to be degraded quickly by human renal dipeptidase, and an inhibitor of this enzyme, probenecid, is included in the fixed dose combination to prolong the actions of sulopenem. The product if approved is intended for the treatment of uUTI with a treatment regimen of one bilayer tablet containing 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil and 500 mg probenecid administered twice a day for 5 days.
L1723: Pivotal toxicology studies that were conducted in support of the NDA in adult animals included 1-month toxicology studies in rats and monkeys with sulopenem etzadroxil and a 14-day combination toxicology study with sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid in rats. There were no
L1724: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1725: toxicity findings of concern, but renal changes were observed in rats. The primary finding observed in adult rats in the 1-month toxicology study was a low incidence of regeneration of proximal tubular epithelium in the kidney accompanied by minimal vacuolation of the renal tubular epithelium, renal tubular hypertrophy, and increased kidney weights. The renal findings are not considered to be clinically relevant due to the limited scope and severity of the findings. The lowest sulopenem etzadroxil dose in rats associated with the kidney findings was 400 mg/kg/day which was associated with a mean plasma area under the curve (AUC) exposure for sulopenem of approximately 9 times the mean clinical AUC exposure for sulopenem following a single oral administration of the bilayer tablet. In the combination sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid toxicology study, kidney weights were increased with an oral sulopenem etzadroxil dose of 800 mg/kg/day administered for 14 days to adult rats, but renal histopathology findings were not observed. These results suggest the duration of sulopenem etzadroxil dosing may influence the severity of renal findings.
L1726: In the definitive juvenile toxicity study, oral administration of sulopenem etzadroxil to juvenile rats for 85 days beginning on postnatal day 5 and continuing to postnatal day 90, was associated with more varied and severe renal histopathology findings compared to the findings in adult rats in the 14-day and 1-month toxicology studies. Renal histopathology in juvenile male and/or female rats included slight degeneration of tubular epithelium, renal infarcts, and intratubular concretions. The findings in juvenile rats occurred at lower sulopenem etzadroxil doses and exposures than the doses associated with renal findings in adult rats in the 1-month study, and the findings were poorly reversible or, in the case of tubular concretions, irreversible after a 2-week recovery period. The renal toxicology results in juvenile rats suggest longer durations of repeated sulopenem etzadroxil dosing may result in more varied and severe renal toxicity with potential clinical relevance. The results are also consistent with a potential for more severe renal toxicity in juvenile rats compared to adults. The sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid bilayer tablet will not be approved for pediatric patients until clinical trials in this population are completed. The results from the juvenile toxicology study suggest increased monitoring of renal toxicity should be considered for future clinical pediatric studies.
L1727: Additional sulopenem etzadroxil-related findings were observed in gastrointestinal (GI) tissues in the 14-day combination toxicology study in rats (mixed cell infiltrates, hyperplasia of glandular epithelium and edema in the large intestine) and the 1-month study in monkeys (minimal mucosal hyperplasia). These effects were reversible and are not considered to be a likely source of serious adverse events (SAEs) for clinical dosing for 5 days with the bilayer tablet. Monkeys also exhibited positive Coombs test results that tended to increase with sulopenem etzadroxil dose and likely contributed to antibody mediation of minimal erythrocyte loss and compensatory erythropoiesis in monkeys. Should a similar reaction to sulopenem etzadroxil occur in humans, it is not expected to produce serious adverse effects over a short 5-day course of treatment with the bilayer tablet, but more concern may be warranted for repeated courses of treatment.
L1728: Both sulopenem etzadroxil and sulopenem were shown to inhibit hERG potassium channels *in vitro* with estimated IC50 values of 33.4 mcM (15.9 µg/ml) and 300 mcM (104.8 µg/ml),
L1729: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1730: respectively. However, concern for inhibition of hERG potassium channels and possible QT prolongation in the clinic is minimal because the 2.64 µg/ml plasma C_{max} for sulopenem associated with administration of a single bilayer tablet containing 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil in fed patients is approximately 6-fold and 40-fold lower than the hERG IC_{50} values for sulopenem etzadroxil and sulopenem, respectively. Also, in a Phase 1 study where no QT prolongation was observed, a single IV dose of 2800 mg sulopenem was associated with a mean plasma C_{max} value (109.7 µg/ml) for sulopenem that was approximately 40 times greater than the expected clinical sulopenem C_{max} associated with oral administration of a single bilayer tablet.
L1731: *In vitro* and *in vivo* genetic toxicology testing was conducted with sulopenem etzadroxil and sulopenem with a similar pattern of results for both compounds. Both compounds were shown to be negative for mutagenicity in Ames assays and sulopenem was negative for mutagenicity in an *in vitro* CHO HGRPT forward mutation assay. However, both compounds produced positive results for clastogenesis in several *in vitro* assays in mammalian cells including an *in vitro* micronucleus assay and human lymphocyte assay with sulopenem etzadroxil and a chromosome aberration assay with sulopenem. These results were balanced by negative results for both compounds *in vivo* in micronucleus assays in bone marrow cells from rats (both compounds) and mice (sulopenem). Based on the negative results in the *in vitro* mutagenicity assays and the *in vivo* micronucleus assays, the weight of evidence supports a negative potential for genotoxicity for sulopenem etzadroxil.
L1732: Sulopenem etzadroxil did not inhibit fertility in male and female rats and was not associated with fetal malformations in embryo-fetal studies in rats and rabbits. However, in mice, a higher litter and fetal incidence of cleft palate in fetuses occurred at a sulopenem etzadroxil dose associated with sulopenem exposures approximately 46-times the mean clinical exposure following a single oral dose of the bilayer tablet. In a pre-postnatal study in rats, sulopenem etzadroxil was not associated with changes in the viability, physical development, neurological development, or reproductive capacity of first-generation offspring.
L1733: Sulopenem and 2-ethylbutyric acid (2-EBA) are released by hydrolysis of sulopenem etzadroxil, and during hydrolysis the formation of formaldehyde is anticipated. However, measurable quantities of formaldehyde were not observed in any of the rat or monkey toxicology studies, although the lower limit of quantitation for formaldehyde in these studies was high, (b)/(4) µg/ml. According to the Applicant, the theoretical maximum amount of formaldehyde expected to form with a 1000 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil is (b)/(4) mg which is substantially lower than the daily body burden of 36 g/day formaldehyde expected to be ingested and formed endogenously. Because the amount of formaldehyde formed through hydrolysis of sulopenem etzadroxil is expected to be much smaller than the normal body burden, the formation of formaldehyde is not a safety concern. The other major metabolite of sulopenem etzadroxil, 2-EBA, had plasma exposures in the nonclinical toxicology studies that often exceeded exposures for sulopenem. 2-EBA is considered to be qualified for safety by its substantial exposures in the general toxicology studies, *in vivo* genetic toxicology studies, and developmental and reproductive toxicology studies with sulopenem etzadroxil. Similarly, two metabolites that
L1734: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1735: occur disproportionately in humans, M1a and M1b, are considered qualified for safety in the rat toxicology studies based on their high percentages in rat plasma.
L1736: Probenecid was first approved in 1951 as BENEMID followed by a number of generic probenecid drug products including the listed probenecid product referenced by the Applicant, PROBENECID by Actavis Pharma, Inc., which is approved for oral doses of up to 1000 mg/day for chronic treatment of gout. In the 14-day combination toxicology study, increasing doses of sulopenem etzadroxil were associated with proportional decreases in probenecid exposure when the two compounds were administered concomitantly. In the same study, probenecid was not associated with notable toxicity and coadministration of probenecid with sulopenem etzadroxil did not substantially change sulopenem AUC exposures in plasma or augment sulopenem etzadroxil-related toxicity. The general toxicity of probenecid is further qualified by its extensive use in FDA-approved products. Information on the product label for the listed probenecid product including warnings, drug interactions, and adverse reactions for probenecid will be included in the labeling for the current product. Information that is missing from the product label for the listed product including information on the nonclinical fertility, embryofetal, and pre-postnatal effects of probenecid will also be absent on the product label for the current product.
L1737: Considering the nonclinical results as a whole, NDA 213972 is considered approvable from a Pharmacology/Toxicology perspective.

L1741: Study Title: Safety Pharmacology – Neurofunctional Assessment of PF-03709270 and PF-03678685 in Sprague Dawley Rats. Study No.: 05GR036.
L1742: Methods: This good laboratory practice (GLP)-compliant study was conducted by [REDACTED] (b) (4) in 2006. Separate groups (6/group of Male Sprague Dawley rats were administered single doses of vehicle (0.5% methylcellulose) or 2000 mg/kg PF-03709270 and PF-03678685 by oral gavage. One hour after dosing, individual animals were evaluated in a functional observational battery including assessments of central nervous system activity and excitability, autonomic nervous system function, neuromuscular function, and sensorimotor function. Locomotor activity and body temperature were also assessed in separate measurements.
L1743: Results: PF-03709270 had no effect on any of the functional observational battery or locomotor assessments and no effect on body temperature compared to control values.

L1745: Study Title: Effect of PF-03709270 on hERG Potassium Channels Stably Expressed in HEK293 Cells. Study No.: PF3709270/GP/0506/HERG
L1746: Methods: This non-GLP compliant study was conducted in 2006 by [REDACTED](b) (4). PF-03709270 dissolved in DMSO was incubated with HEK293 cells stably transfected with hERG encoded potassium channels in concentrations of 3, 30, and 100 \muM. A positive control agent was not tested.
L1747: Results: PF-03709270 inhibited HERG currents by 5.1\pm 1.6\%, 48.3\pm 2.2\% and 75.8\pm 2.6\% at 3, 30 and 100 \muM, respectively. The inhibition observed was dose dependent. Using these values, an IC_{50} value of 33.4 \muM was determined for hERG inhibition by PF-03709270.

A positive control agent, dofetilide (30 nM) was tested under the same conditions.

Administrations followed a cross-over design with a 1-week washout period between administrations. Before dosing, monkeys were implanted with radio-telemetry transmitters. In addition to clinical signs and toxicokinetic measurements (whole blood was collected pre-dose and approximately 8 hours after dosing), telemetry measurements of heart rate, systemic arterial blood pressure (systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure) and electrocardiogram parameters (resting rate, PR, QRS, and QT intervals) were measured pre-dose and at approximately 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 22 hours after dosing. The method for calculating QTc values was not identified in the study report.
L1753: Results: PF-03709270 treated animals experienced emesis within 8 hours of dosing (6/8 animals) and all animals had loose stool beginning at 24 hours after dosing with normal stool returning by 96 hours after dosing. In animals treated with PF-03709270, there was a significant decrease in the mean PR interval from baseline (-6 msec) at 22 hours after dosing compared to control values (-1 msec from baseline). Metabolism
Effect of CP-070,429 on Human Drug Metabolizing Enzymes In Vitro./	CP-70429 was incubated in seven concentrations ranging from 0.159 to 50.0 mM with pooled human liver microsomes and substrates specific for different CYP isozymes. CP-70429 demonstrated little or no inhibition of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, or CYP3A.
Study No.: DM2006-070429-029	
In Vitro Characterization of Sulopenem and Sulopenem Etzadroxil as Inhibitors of Cytochrome P450 Enzymes in Human Liver Microsomes/	Sulopenem and sulopenem etzadroxil were separately incubated in concentrations ranging from 0.206 to 150 mM with pooled human liver microsomes and substrates for specific CYP isozymes in assays measuring direct and time-dependent CYP enzyme activity. Sulopenem did not inhibit any of the tested CYP isozymes (CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6 and CYP3A4/5) directly or in a time-dependent manner at any concentration. Sulopenem etzadroxil showed weak direct inhibition of CYP3A4/5 at the highest concentrations tested and the IC50 was estimated to be >150 mM. Also, at the highest concentrations, sulopenem etzadroxil demonstrated a weak time-dependent inhibition of CYP3A4/5.

Profiling and Identification of Metabolites in Urine and Plasma Following Intravenous Administration of [14C]CP-70,429 to Cynomolgus Monkeys/ Study No.: DM2006-070429-027	One female and one male Cynomolgus monkey were administered a single dose of 200 mg/kg [14C]CP-70429 by intravenous injection. Radioactivity recovered in the urine accounted for 28.07% in the male and 30.47% in the female. Radioactivity recovered in the feces accounted for 35.65% in the male and 33.55% in the female.

L1815: Type of Study	Major Findings
A 14-Day Oral Gavage Toxicity Study of PF-03709270 With and Without Probenecid in Rats with a 14-Day Recovery Period/ Study No.: 18IT001(b) (4) - 417503-02	
Sprague-Dawley rats were administered vehicle or PF-03709270 with and without probenecid in the following groups in daily oral gavage doses for 14 days: Group 1 (vehicle for PF-03709270), Group 2 (vehicle and 200 mg/kg probenecid), Group 3 (100 mg/kg PF-03709270), Group 4 (800 mg/kg PF-03709270), Group 5 (100 mg/kg PF-03709270 and 200 mg/kg probenecid), Group 6 (800 mg/kg PF-03709270 and 200 mg/kg probenecid).
CP-70429 Plasma Toxicokinetics (Table 18)
Dose Proportionality: Plasma AUC values for CP-70429 increased in an approximately dose-proportional manner and plasma C_{max} values increased in a less than dose-proportional manner.
Plasma Accumulation: AUC values were relatively similar after the first dose compared to after 14 days of dosing consistent with limited plasma accumulation with repeated dosing.
2-Ethylbutyric Acid (2-EBA) Plasma Toxicokinetics (Table 19)
Dose Proportionality: Plasma AUC values for 2-EBA increased in a more than dose-proportional manner and plasma C_{max} values increased in a less than dose-proportional manner.
Plasma Accumulation: AUC values were relatively similar after the first dose compared to after 14 days of dosing suggesting a limited plasma accumulation of 2-EBA with repeated dosing.
Ratio of CP-70429 to 2-EBA: Plasma AUC values for CP-70429 were as much as 2-fold lower than those for 2-EBA.
Probenecid Plasma Toxicokinetics (Table 20)
Plasma Accumulation: Probenecid C_{max} and AUC values were generally similar on Days 1 and 14 with little evidence of plasma accumulation.
Effect of Concomitant Probenecid on CP-70429 Exposures:
Plasma AUC exposures to CP-70429 in males and females were approximately 1.5 higher for both sexes in the 800:200 mg/kg/day PF-03709270:probenecid group (Group 6) compared to the 800 mg/kg/day PF-03709270 group (Group 4). However the AUC exposure for the lower-dose combination group, 100:200 PF-03709270:probenecid (Group 5) was the same or less than comparable exposures for males and females in the 100 mg/kg/day PF-03709270 group (Group 3). This pattern is consistent with probenecid having a slightly more pronounced effect on the renal elimination of higher plasma exposures of CP-70429.
Effect of Concomitant PF-03709270 on Probenecid Exposures: Probenecid exposures reduced in a PF-03709270 dose-dependent manner. This pattern suggests PF-03709270 may have increased the plasma clearance of probenecid.

L1863: ## 5.5. Toxicology
L1864: ## 5.5.1. General Toxicology
L1865: Study title/ number: 1-Month Oral Toxicity and Micronucleus Study of PF-03709270 in Rats/
Study No: 06GR278
L1866: - Based on minimal vacuolation of the renal tubular epithelium, renal tubular hypertrophy, and a low incidence of tubular regeneration that occurred primarily in high-dose males and females and to a lesser extent in mid-dose males, the low-dose of 100 mg/kg/day was identified as a no observed adverse effect level (NOAEL) in this study.
- The plasma AUC0-24h for CP-70429 (sulopenem) associated with the NOAEL dose of PF-03709270 on Day 30 was 7240 ng•hr/ml.
- The oral administration of PF-03709270 to rats did not induce micronuclei in the polychromatic bone marrow erythrocytes at ≤2000 mg/kg.

L1873: **Table 37. Observations and Results: Changes From Control (Study No.: 06GR278)**
L1874: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	One HD male was euthanized on Day 23 due to body weight loss and clinical signs including rough fur, stained fur, decreased skin turgor, and noisy labored respiration observed on Days 19 to 23.
Clinical Signs	In the HD group, clinical signs included stained fur of the muzzle, urogenital and/or anogenital region in 7/20 animals, noisy respiration in 3/20 animals, and loose stools in 1/20 animals. The observations were observed sporadically with low incidence throughout the study.
Body Weights	No PF-03709270-related effects on body weight were observed.
Feed Consumption	Except on Day 8 where slight decreases in mean food consumption (-11% to -12%) were observed in MD and HD females and HD males, no changes in food consumption occurred.
Ophthalmoscopy	No PF-03709270-related ophthalmoscopy findings were observed.
Hematology	Day 31
HD males: +40% mean prothrombin time**
The increased mean prothrombin time occurred only in HD males and was not considered to be toxicologically important.
Clinical Chemistry	No toxicologically relevant changes in serum chemistry were observed. Mean values for ALT and AST were statistically significantly decreased compared to control values in HD and/or MD males and HD females.
Urinalysis	No toxicologically relevant urinalysis findings were observed
Gross Pathology	Gross pathology findings included enlarged cecum and/or pale multi-focal discoloration of the kidney in 1/10 LD males, 4/10 MD males, 2/10 MD females, and 9/10 HD males. In 9/10 HD females, enlarged cecum was observed including one female with dilation of the duodenum.
Organ Weights	Kidney: Relative kidney weights (relative to body weight) were increased approximately 10% and 40% in both sexes in the MD and HD groups respectively compared to control values. The increased kidney weights correlated with renal tubular hypertrophy observed microscopically.
Liver: Mean absolute and relative liver weights were increased 10% -20% in both sexes in the HD group compared to control values.
Spleen: Absolute and relative spleen weights were significantly decreased by 13-14% in HD females compared to control values.
Prostate: Absolute and relative prostate weights were decreased approximately 20% in MD and HD males.
In the absence of histologic correlates, the changes in liver, spleen, and prostate weights were not considered to be toxicologically important.
L1875: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1876: Parameters	Major Findings
Histopathology
Adequate battery: Yes	Minimal focal vacuolation of segmental tubular epithelial cells in the renal cortex occurred in 5/10 HD males and 5/10 HD females and in 1/10 MD females. All HD males and 5/10 HD females at 2000 mg/kg exhibited minimal to mild tubular hypertrophy of the outer stripe of the medullary zone of the kidney. The tubular hypertrophy was characterized by mild dilation of the tubular lumina with increased amounts of epithelial cytoplasm sometimes accompanied by multiple foci of epithelial regeneration. The severity was minimal to mild in HD males and mild in HD females. Fewer males (2/10) and females (1/10) in the MD group and 1/10 male in the LD group exhibited this same change. Tubular hypertrophy correlated with the increased kidney weights for males and females at the two highest dose levels. Immunohistochemical staining for P450 enzymes 3A1, 2B6, and 2E1 in kidney sections from one control male and one HD male showed increased intensity of staining in the hypertrophic outer stripe zone in the HD male consistent with metabolic enzyme induction.
[Other evaluations]	Micronucleus assay: see Section 5.5.3
Toxicokinetics: see Section 5.4

L1886: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1887: **Table 39. Observations and Results: Changes From Control (Study No.: 06GR263)**
L1888: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	No mortality occurred during the study period.
Clinical Signs	PF-03709270-related clinical signs included loose/liquid stools and emesis, and with a lower incidence, distended abdomen. Loose/liquid stools were observed beginning on Day 1 in all dose groups and persisted with dose-dependent increases in incidence and severity throughout the dosing period. Sporadic emesis was observed in all dose groups between Day 1 and 26. Abdominal distention was observed in one MD male (Days 30-31), and two HD males (Days 5-12 and 16-31 for one animal and Days 2-12 for the other) and one HD female (Days 28-30). Hunched posture was observed in one HD male (Days 8-9 and 11-12) and one HD female (Day 10) possibly secondary to the gastrointestinal observations.
Body Weights	Body weights were decreased at the end of the dosing period in HD males and females by approximately 16% and 9%, respectively, compared to control values.
Feed Consumption	Delays in eating and decreases in food consumption (qualitatively assessed) were observed beginning on Day 2 in MD and HD males and females.
Ophthalmoscopy	No PF-03709270-related ophthalmoscopy findings were observed.
ECG	No PF-03709270-related changes in any ECG parameters, blood pressure, or heart rate were observed.
Hematology	On Day 15, minimal to mild decreases in RBC, HGB, and/or HCT (reduced 15% to 19% compared to pretreatment values) were observed in individual HD monkeys. On Day 30, slightly greater, but generally mild, decreases in group mean values for these parameters (reduced 14% to 23% compared to pretreatment values) were noted in HD monkeys and in MD females as well as increased RDW (red cell distribution width, 10-20% higher than pretreatment values) and absolute and percent reticulocytes (240% to 550% increases compared to pretreatment values). Direct Coomb's testing on Days 15 and 30 demonstrated positive reactions for polyspecific anti-human globulin and anti-IgG, but not anti-C3b/C3d, in all MD and HD animals and the strength of the reaction tended to increase with dose. These results were consistent with antibody-mediated red blood cell loss with compensatory erythropoiesis. Slightly increased platelet counts (40% to 60% increase compared to pretreatment values) on Days 15 and 30 in male HD monkeys was consistent with thrombocytosis secondary to antibody-mediated red cell turnover.
Clinical Chemistry	In HD males and females, slight reductions in mean serum albumin (reductions of 14% to 18% compared to pretreatment values) were observed. The reduction in serum albumin coupled with slightly increased serum globulin in HD females (+10% compared to pretreatment values) resulted in a decreased albumin/globulin ratio (-24% compared to pretreatment). These systemic responses may have been associated with immune-mediated red cell turnover.
Urinalysis	On Day 31, urine pH was slightly decreased to \le 8.0 in 0/6, 1/6, 4/6, and 3/6 animals (both male and female) in control, LD, MD, and HD groups, respectively. A white precipitate, possibly related to the alkaline urine was observed on Day 31 in urine samples from three HD females. The sediment had a microscopic appearance of amorphous granular material consisting of round, oval and irregularly shaped refractile bodies. The origin and toxicological significance of the granular material is unknown.
Gross Pathology	Dilation of the colon was observed in 2/3 HD males.
L1889: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L1890: Parameters	Major Findings
Organ Weights	
In males and females in the HD group, absolute and relative (to body weight) liver weights were increased by approximately 10-30% compared to control values. Also absolute and relative kidney weights were increased by approximately 8-9% in HD males. All of the changes were not statistically significant and no histological correlates corresponded with the increased liver and kidney weights.
Mean absolute and relative (to body weight) adrenal weights were increased by 10 to 40% in MD and HD males and in females at all PF-03709270 dose levels. In HD animals increased adrenal weights were associated with cortical hypertrophy. Also absolute and relative thymus weights were decreased by 26% to 72% compared to control values in MD and HD males and females. The decreased thymus weights correlated with histological findings of lymphoid depletion in the thymus. The increased adrenal weights and decreased thymus weights are consistent with treatment-related stress.

Histopathology	
No liver or kidney histopathology was reported.
GI tract: In the jejunum and, to a lesser extent, the ileum, minimal mucosal hyperplasia was noted in HD animals. The effects were subtle and likely reflected a slight increase in cell loss from villi and increased proliferation of crypt epithelium.
Adrenal Glands and Thymus: Decreased cortical hypertrophy in HD animals and lymphoid depletion in HD males (minimal to marked) and females (moderate to marked) was consistent with a treatment-related stress response.

[Other evaluations]	Toxicokinetics: See Section 5.4

L1892: ## 5.5.2. General Toxicology; Additional Studies
L1893: Study title/ number: 14-Day Oral Gavage Toxicity Study of PF-03709270 with and without Probenecid in Rats with a 14-Day Recovery Period/ Study No: 18IT001-(b) (4)-417503-02
L1894: - In male and female rats administered 800 mg/kg PF-03709270 with and without probenecid, histopathology findings included accumulations of seromucinous secretions along with degeneration of the nasal epithelium and slight osteolysis of turbinate bones. The nasal findings were reduced for incidence and severity after the recovery period and may have been related to nasal reflux exposure to gavage fluids.
- Histopathology findings in the large intestine of male and female rats receiving 800 mg/kg/day PF-03709270 with or without probenecid included infiltrates of mixed inflammatory cells and hyperplasia of the glandular epithelium. The large intestine findings were fully reversible after the recovery period.
- Concomitant administration of 200 mg/kg/day probenecid with 800 mg/kg/day PF-03709270 did not substantially change PF-03709270-related findings.

L1900: **Table 41. Observations and Results: Changes From Control (Study No.: 18IT001-(b) (4)-417503-02)**
L1901: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	All animals survived until the scheduled euthanasia date.
Clinical Signs	No clinical signs related to PF-03709270 or probenecid were observed.
Body Weights	Body weights were similar in all groups for males and females.
Feed Consumption	No change in food consumption was observed.
Ophthalmoscopy	No toxicologically relevant ophthalmoscopy findings were observed.
Hematology	No changes related to test-article administration were observed.
Clinical Chemistry	Urea Nitrogen: Statistically significantly lower urea nitrogen levels in serum were observed in males and females in Groups 4 (800 mg/kg PF-03709270) and Group 6 (800 mg/kg PF-03709270:200 mg/kg probenecid) at the end of dosing on Day 15. In males, urea nitrogen levels were decreased by 29% and 25% in Groups 4 and 6, respectively, and in females urea nitrogen levels were decreased by 20% and 25% in the same respective groups. At the end of the recovery period on Day 30, urea nitrogen levels were similar in all groups.
Creatinine: Serum creatinine was statistically significantly increased in Groups 5 (100 mg/kg PF-03709270: 200 mg probenecid) and 6 in males and females at the end of dosing on Day 15. In males, serum creatinine levels were 28% and 32% increased, and in females creatinine levels were approximately 9% and 6% increased respectively in Groups 5 and 6 on Day 15. On Day 30 after the recovery period, creatinine levels were similar in all groups.
Renal impairment generally results in increased circulating levels of both urea nitrogen and creatinine. In this case urea nitrogen levels were reduced in the groups receiving the highest doses of PF-03709270. Reductions in urea nitrogen might indicate that less is being produced by the liver. Given the reversibility of the findings and in the absence of histological correlates in the liver or kidney, the toxicological relevance of the findings is not clear.
Urinalysis	Urine specific gravity was significantly higher for females in Group 6 (1.050) compared to the mean control value (1.025) at the end of dosing on Day 15. However, a similar effect was not observed in males in Group 6 or in the other treatment groups on Day 15 and specific gravity values were similar in all groups for both sexes at the end of the recovery period on Day 29.
Gross Pathology	No gross pathology findings were considered to be related to administration of PF-03709270 or probenecid or the combination.

L1994: Parameters	Major Findings
Feed Consumption	
Males: HD males demonstrated treatment-related, statistically significant decreased food consumption of up to 42% compared to animals in the vehicle control group. MD males also experienced transient decreases (13-22%) in food consumption on Treatment Days 4 and 8.

HD females demonstrated a statistically significant increase in estrous cycle length (4.44 days compared to 4.05 days for the controls), and a decrease in the number of estrous cycles (3.38 estrous cycles compared to 3.75 estrous cycles in the controls). There were no significant PF-03709270-related effects on the number of corpora lutea, implantation sites, resorptions, and pre- and post-implantation losses. HD females experienced a statistically significant decrease in the number of viable fetuses (14.7 compared to 16.4 in the vehicle controls), however both numbers fell within historical control range (12.4 to 16.7).

Enlarged gallbladder was also observed in two of the HD females with enlarged stomachs/intestines. Pregnancy occurred in 23/25, 25/25, 24/25, and 22/25 female mice in the vehicle control, LD, MD, and HD groups, respectively. Because 9/22 pregnant females in the HD group died or were euthanized in extremis prematurely, only 13/22 HD females underwent Caesarean section on GD 18. No caesarean section parameters were affected by dosages of PF-03709270 as high as 2000 mg/kg/day. The litter averages for corpora lutea, implantations, litter sizes, live fetuses, early and late resorptions, the percentage of resorbed conceptuses, and the percentage of live male fetuses were similar in all groups. There were no dead fetuses and all placenta appeared normal.
Necropsy findings
Offspring	Mean fetal weights at birth were significantly reduced for male and female offspring and for pooled results for both sexes in the HD group. All of the HD values were at or below the nadir of the historical control range (Table 48).

L2032: **Table 50. Observations and Results (Study No.: 08GR040)**
L2033: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	Deaths considered to be related to PF-03709270 administration included one HD female euthanized on GD 10 due to excess body weight loss and one HD female found dead on GD 19.
Clinical Signs	PF-03709270-related clinical signs in most HD females consisted of alopecia, stained fur, hunched stance, and noisy respiration. In the MD group, the only treatment-related clinical sign was noisy respiration in 2 animals.
Body Weights	Statistically significant PF-03709270-related reductions in maternal body weight and body weight gain were noted in the MD and HD groups. In the HD group, body weight gain over the dosing period (GD 6-18) was reduced by 42% and mean body weights were significantly reduced from GD 8 to GD 21 by 4-14% compared to control values. The effect was less pronounced in the MD group where body weight gain over the dosing period (GD 6-18) was significantly reduced by 17%, and mean body weights were significantly reduced from GD 14 to GD 21 by 3-6%. In the LD group, body weight gain over the entire treatment period (GD 6-18) was greater than that noted in the control group.
Feed Consumption	PF-03709270-related decreases in food consumption were noted in the MD and HD groups with significant 12% and 30% reductions over the treatment period for the two dose groups respectively. In the LD group a statistically significant decrease in food consumption was noted from GD 7-9 (11% reduction compared to control), however, food consumption over the entire treatment period was comparable to controls.
Necropsy findings
Cesarean Section Data	No PF-03709270-related gross pathology findings were observed. Gravid uterus weights were significantly decreased in the MD and HD groups, and in the same groups, non-significant PF-03709270-related increases in the number of early resorptions and post-implantation losses and decreases in the number of viable fetuses were noted. Also, mean fetal body weights were significantly reduced by 11% in the HD group (5.09 g) compared to the mean control value (5.72 g). There were no treatment-related effects on any Cesarean section parameters in the LD group.
Necropsy findings
Offspring	External Alterations: The only reported external malformation was an omphalocele in a single LD fetus.
Visceral Alterations: None of the visceral malformations were statistically significantly increased for litter or fetal incidence in the PF-03709270-treatment groups compared to control values. Two malformations that did not occur in the vehicle control group occurred in single fetuses in the MD (single fetus with situs inversus) and the HD groups (single fetus with retroesophageal aortic arch). There were no PF-03709270-related increases in visceral variations.
Skeletal Alterations: No skeletal malformations were reported. Two skeletal variations, unossified cervical centrum and unossified metatarsal, were statistically significantly increased for litter incidence in the HD group compared to the vehicle control group.

L2048: Parameters	Major Findings
Body Weights	
No significant differences in mean body weights were observed for any of the PF-03709270 treatment groups. In HD dams, there were statistically significant decreases in body weight gain over the gestation intervals of GD 7 to GD 10 (reduced 133% compared to control values), GD 20 to GD 23 (reduced 83% compared to control values), and for the entire dosing period from GD 7 to GD 20 (reduced 60% compared to control values). In the MD group, a statistically significant decrease in body weight gain was noted over the gestation interval of GD 20 to GD 23 (reduced 50% compared to control values) and for the entire dosing period GD 7 to 20 (reduced 36% compared to control values). In the LD group, body weight gains were significantly decreased over the entire dosing period from GD 7-20 (reduced 28% compared to control values).

Feed Consumption	
Average maternal food consumption in the MD and HD groups was statistically significantly reduced daily from GD 8-22 and over the intervals of 8-10, 11-13, 14-16, 17-20, and 8-20. In the LD group, food consumption was significantly reduced daily from GD 13-22 and over the intervals of 8-10, 14-16, 17-20, and 8-20. Average daily food consumption was significantly reduced in all the PF-03709270 treatment groups over the dosing period (GD 8 to GD 20) with dose-dependent reductions in daily food intake of 15%, 36% and 44% compared to control values for the LD, MD, and HD groups, respectively. For the GD 23 to 29 interval, food consumption was similar in all groups.

Necropsy findings
Cesarean Section Data	
No maternal necropsy findings were considered related to PF-03709270 administration. In the MD and HD groups, late resorptions were increased compared to control values with statistical significance achieved for the HD group. Also, post-implantation loss was significantly increased and the number of viable fetuses, and gravid uterine weights were significantly reduced in the MD and HD groups compared to control values. Mean fetal body weights were significantly reduced by approximately 9% and 7% in the MD and HD groups respectively with mean values of 39.75, 39.50, 36.30, and 37.09 grams for the control, LD, MD, and HD groups, respectively.

Necropsy findings
Offspring	
External Alterations: No external malformations were considered related to administration of PF-03709270. Two external malformations were reported: exencephaly in one vehicle control fetus and omphalocele in one MD fetus.
Visceral Alterations: No visceral malformations were reported. Multiple visceral variations occurred with similar incidences in all groups.
Skeletal Malformations: There were no PF-03709270-related skeletal malformations. Malformations (fused frontal, nasal, rib, and sternebra; absent interparietal, supraoccipital, and thoracic arch; hemicentric thoracic centrum; and misshapen parietal) were either seen only in the concurrent control group or at incidence levels comparable to or below the concurrent control group.
Skeletal Variations: Multiple skeletal variations were observed but only one variation was increased for incidence in a dose-dependent manner. The litter incidence of unossified forepaw phalanx was statistically significantly increased in both the MD group (litter incidence of 72.2%) and HD group (litter incidence of 84.6%) compared to the LD (litter incidence of 23.5%) and control (litter incidence of 21.1%) groups. This variation may have resulted from maternal toxicity and is consistent with the reduced fetal body weights observed in the MD and HD groups in this study.

L2074: ## 5.5.6. Other Toxicology Studies
L2075: Study title/ number: Juvenile Toxicity and Toxicokinetic Oral Gavage and Intravenous Injection Study With Sulopenem and PF-03709270 in Sprague-Dawley Rats With up to a 4 Week Recovery Period/ Study No.: 181T001-8383182-02
L2076: ## Key Findings
L2077: - Kidney histopathology including tubular epithelial degeneration and tubular concretions occurred in juvenile rats with the lowest administered dose of sulopenem IV dose (60 mg/kg/day). Tubular concretions were present after a 2-week recovery period. The same pattern of kidney histopathology was evident with the lowest administered dose of oral PF-03709270 (25 mg/kg/day).
- No effects on sexual maturation and bone development, were caused by IV sulopenem doses up to 200 mg/kg/day or by oral PF-03709270 in doses up to 225 mg/kg/day. Neurological function in juvenile rats was also unaffected except for a delayed reduction in overall movement that occurred weeks after the end of dosing.
- Because poorly reversible kidney histopathology was evident with the lowest administered doses of IV sulopenem and oral PF-03709270 in juvenile rats, no NOAEL values were assigned in this study.

L2123: ## 6. Clinical Pharmacology
L2124: ## 6.1. Executive Summary
L2125: The Office of Clinical Pharmacology (Division of Infectious Disease Pharmacology and Division of Pharmacometrics) has reviewed the information contained in NDA 213972. See Table 64 for a summary of clinical pharmacology-related recommendations and comments on key review issues.
L2126: **Table 64. Summary of OCP's Recommendations and Comments on Key Issues**
L2127: Review Issue	Recommendations and Comments
Pivotal or supportive evidence of effectiveness	The pivotal evidence of effectiveness for sulopenem in patients with uncomplicated urinary tract infections (uUTI) comes from one Phase 3 trial (IT001-301).
General dosing instructions	The proposed dosing regimen is one bilayer tablet (500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil/500 mg probenecid) administered orally with food twice daily for 5 days. Probenecid increases the plasma exposures of sulopenem while decreasing its renal clearance. Because of the importance of urine drug concentrations in the treatment of uUTI, use of probenecid in combination with sulopenem etzadroxil may not be appropriate for the proposed indication. Nonclinical PK/PD studies also suggest the proposed dosage regimen may not be optimal.
Dosing in patient subgroups (intrinsic and extrinsic factors)	No dosage adjustment is needed in patients with hepatic impairment. Use is not recommended in patients with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min due to reduced effectiveness. Use is also not recommended in subjects on hemodialysis due to the unknown impact of hemodialysis on the disposition of sulopenem.
Labeling	The contents and format of the proposed labeling language are not aligned with the current guidance and will be revised.
L2128: Abbreviations: CL_{Cr}, creatinine clearance; PD, pharmacodynamics; PK, pharmacokinetics
L2129: ## 6.2. Summary of Clinical Pharmacology Assessment
L2130: ## 6.2.1. Pharmacology and Clinical Pharmacokinetics
L2131: **Table 65. Summary of the Pharmacokinetic Properties of Sulopenem**
L2132: ## **Absorption**
L2133: Sulopenem etzadroxil is a prodrug that is rapidly hydrolyzed to sulopenem, the microbiologically-active moiety, following oral administration. Only the pharmacokinetic profile of sulopenem is discussed further because sulopenem etzadroxil is not detected in plasma following oral administration. The absolute bioavailability of sulopenem following administration of a single dose of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil and 500 mg probenecid as the oral bilayer tablet under fasted conditions was 40%. Peak plasma concentrations are achieved within 1 h under fasted conditions and 2 h under fed conditions. A high fat meal increased the oral bioavailability of sulopenem to 64%.
L2134: ## **Distribution**
L2135: % bound to human plasma protein	10.7%
Volume of distribution (L)a	75 L (following intravenous administration) and 134 L (apparent Vd after oral administration)
L2136: ## **Elimination**
L2137: The half-life of sulopenem is approximately 1.2 hours.
L2138: ## **Metabolism**
L2139: Sulopenem etzadroxil is rapidly hydrolyzed after oral administration to sulopenem in the intestines and in systemic circulation. Sulopenem and two inactive metabolites formed by \beta-lactam cyclic amide bond hydrolysis (M1a and M1b) are the major circulating entities. Sulopenem, M1a and M1b accounted for 32%, 21.8% and 43.6%, respectively, of circulating radioactivity in the mass balance study. No metabolism of sulopenem was observed *in vitro* with recombinant CYP or UGT enzymes.
L2140: ## **Excretion**
L2141: Following oral administration of a 2000 mg dose of [14C] sulopenem etzadroxil, 85.1% of the radiolabeled dose was recovered in urine (44.3%) and feces (40.8%) as unchanged sulopenem and metabolites. Sulopenem accounted for 26.9% and 3.1% of the administered dose in urine and feces, respectively.
L2142: a Mean value based on a single dose of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil/500 mg probenecid in healthy volunteers for apparent volume of distribution after oral administration
L2143: ## 6.2.2. General Dosing and Therapeutic Individualization
L2144: ## General Dosing
L2145: The Applicant's proposed dosage regimen is one bilayer tablet (containing 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil/500 mg probenecid) administered orally twice daily for 5 days based on the expectation that as a \beta-lactam, sulopenem should exhibit time dependent killing. However, data from the Applicant's nonclinical PK/PD studies suggest that sulopenem's activity against uropathogens may be concentration dependent, which would imply that the proposed dosage regimen is not optimal. If sulopenem's activity is indeed concentration dependent, a higher dose would be expected to be more efficacious than the proposed dosage regimen.
L2146: ## Therapeutic Individualization
L2147: No clinically significant differences in the PK of sulopenem were observed based on age, gender, or body weight.
L2148: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2149: ## Hepatic Impairment
L2150: The effect of hepatic impairment on the PK of sulopenem was not studied. However, because sulopenem does not undergo significant hepatic metabolism or biliary excretion, hepatic impairment is not expected to impact the PK of sulopenem.
L2151: ## Renal Impairment
L2152: The sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid fixed-dose combination is not recommended in patients with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min and patients on hemodialysis.
L2153: The dedicated renal impairment study showed AUC values of sulopenem for subjects with mild, moderate and severe renal impairment were 2.0-, 3.0- and 7.4-fold higher, respectively, than the corresponding exposure in subjects with normal renal function after receiving a single 1000 mg oral dose of sulopenem etzadroxil. These increases in sulopenem plasma exposure paralleled a progressive decrease in sulopenem renal clearance with worsening renal impairment. However, because sulopenem has a short half-life (~1 h), the cumulative amount of sulopenem recovered in urine over a 24 h period was comparable across renal function groups. Although the effect of probenecid on sulopenem exposure was not evaluated in this study, probenecid's functionality as an OAT3 inhibitor is attenuated in the setting of renal impairment, and thus is not expected to yield significant increases in sulopenem exposures in subjects with renal impairment. The effects of kidney failure (CL_{Cr} &lt; 15 mL/min) and hemodialysis on the PK of sulopenem were not studied.
L2154: Given the proposed uUTI indication, renal impairment has implications for both safety and efficacy. The safety assessment for subjects across renal function groups indicated that no additional treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were observed in the various renal impairment groups compared with subjects with normal renal function. The AUC observed in subjects with severe renal impairment was comparable to the AUC associated with the maximally tolerated dose (MTD) in single ascending doses (SAD) studies, and ~28% higher than the AUC observed for the MTD in multiple ascending doses (MAD) studies. Nonetheless, given sulopenem's short half-life and the proposed treatment duration of 5 days, 500 mg sulopenem administered with 500 mg probenecid is expected to be safe in subjects with severe renal impairment. This was confirmed in the Phase 3 uUTI trial, where no additional TEAEs were observed in subjects with severe renal impairment (See Section 8.2).
L2155: Based on the available safety information, the fixed-dose combination is not recommended in patients with CL_{Cr} &lt; 15 mL/min and patients on hemodialysis because the safety of sulopenem has not been studied in these subpopulations.
L2156: In the Phase 3 uUTI trial, the efficacy of sulopenem was lower in subjects with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min compared to subjects with CL_{Cr} &gt; 60 mL/min (See Section 8.1.2). This decreased response to sulopenem may be partly due to the reduced renal clearance of sulopenem (and subsequently, lower urine sulopenem concentrations especially early in the dosing interval) in subjects with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min. Therefore, the fixed-dose combination is not recommended in patients with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min due to sulopenem's reduced effectiveness in this subpopulation.
L2157: ## Outstanding Issues
L2158: None
L2159: ## 6.3. Comprehensive Clinical Pharmacology Review
L2160: ## 6.3.1. General Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics
L2161: Information pertaining to the general pharmacology and pharmacokinetic characteristics of sulopenem are summarized in Table 66. Relevant clinical pharmacology information is also summarized for sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid in Table 66.
L2162: **Table 66. General Pharmacology and Pharmacokinetic Characteristics**
L2163: Characteristic	Summary
Mechanism of Action	Sulopenem etzadroxil is an oral prodrug that is rapidly cleaved to release the active compound, sulopenem. Sulopenem belongs to the penem (\beta-lactam) class of antibacterial drugs. Sulopenem inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding to essential penicillin-binding proteins (PBP). Probenecid is a uricosuric and renal tubular blocking agent that inhibits the OAT3-mediated excretion of sulopenem, thereby providing increased plasma concentrations of sulopenem.
Active Moieties	Sulopenem
QT Prolongation	At a concentration of 40 times or greater than that achieved after a single 500 mg dose, sulopenem does not prolong the QTc interval to any clinically relevant extent.
Bioanalysis	Multiple LC-MS/MS assays were developed and validated to determine concentrations of sulopenem in human plasma and urine. All bioanalytical methods met the requirements for accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and specificity.
Drug exposure at the therapeutic dosing regimen for uUTI	The mean (%CV) of AUC_{0-inf} and C_{max} following single dose administration of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil with 500 mg probenecid in healthy subjects were 5.00 (25.3%) \mug\cdoth/mL and 1.84 (39.1%) \mug/mL, respectively, under fasted conditions. AUC_{0-inf} and C_{max} increased to 7.41 (22.7%) \mug\cdoth/mL and 2.66 (43.6%) \mug/mL, respectively, under fed conditions.
Based on a population pharmacokinetic analysis, model predicted AUC_{0-12h} and C_{max} following administration of a single dose containing 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil with 500 mg probenecid in uUTI patients were 4.87 (33.9%) \mug\cdoth/mL and 1.39 (30.6%) \mug/mL, respectively.
Of note, the model-predicted sulopenem AUC and C_{max} for Phase 3 uUTI patients are based on composite PK data from subjects reported as having received the fixed-dose bilayer tablet in either the fed or fasted state. Fed status was poorly defined in the Phase 3 study and food intake was not reported for all subjects. Because food increases bioavailability and food intake was variable, delineating the influence of infection on sulopenem exposures is confounded by this lack of uniformity in study drug administration.
L2164: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2165: Characteristic	Summary
Range of effective dose or exposure	No dose-ranging studies were conducted. The Phase 3 uUTI study evaluated a single regimen of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil/500 mg probenecid twice a day.
Maximally tolerated dose (MTD) or exposure	4000 mg is considered the maximally tolerated single dose based on SAD studies. 1200 mg sulopenem etzadroxil in combination with 1000 mg probenecid administered BID for 10 days was the maximally tolerated dose in MAD studies.
Dose Proportionality	The AUC of sulopenem increased in an approximately dose proportional manner for single doses of 400 mg to 2000 mg. C_{max} increased less than dose proportionally with increasing doses.
Variability	For the to-be-marketed bilayer tablet, inter-subject variability (%CV) in AUC_{0-inf} and C_{max} were 25.3% and 39.1%, respectively, for single dose administration of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil in combination with 500 mg probenecid in healthy subjects under fasted conditions. Under fed conditions, %CV in AUC_{0-inf} and C_{max} were 22.7% and 43.6%, respectively.
Based on population pharmacokinetic analysis, model predicted %CV in AUC_{0-12h} and C_{max} were 33.9% and 30.6%, respectively, in uUTI patients administered a single dose of 500 mg sulopenem in combination with 500 mg probenecid.
Food effect	Coadministration of the to-be-marketed sulopenem etzadroxil bilayer tablet with a high fat meal increases sulopenem AUC_{0-inf} and C_{max} by 48% and 45%, respectively.
Inhibition/Induction of metabolism [in vitro]	Although sulopenem etzadroxil is not detected in plasma following oral administration, it has the potential to inhibit CYP enzymes and transporters located in the gut. In vitro, sulopenem etzadroxil is an inhibitor of CYP3A4/5. However, because it is rapidly hydrolyzed to sulopenem, clinically relevant DDIs are not expected with CYP3A4/5 substrates.
Substrate transporter systems [in vitro]	Sulopenem is a substrate of OAT3.
Probenecid is a substrate of BCRP.
Sulopenem etzadroxil is a substrate of P-gp. In a clinical DDI study with a P-gp inhibitor (itraconazole), the effect on the AUC and C_{max} of sulopenem was not clinically significant.
Inhibition/Induction of transporter systems	Sulopenem etzadroxil is an inhibitor of BCRP and P-gp. Because it is rapidly hydrolyzed to sulopenem, clinically relevant DDIs are not expected with BCRP and P-gp substrates.
L2166: Probenecid is an inhibitor of OAT3 and BCRP in vitro.

L2168: ## 6.3.2. Clinical Pharmacology Questions
L2169: Does the clinical pharmacology program provide supportive evidence of effectiveness?
L2170: The primary evidence of efficacy of sulopenem in the treatment of uUTI was provided by one Phase 3 trial (IT001-301). In accordance with the FDA guidance on drug development for the treatment of uUTI, the Applicant evaluated sulopenem urine concentrations in a subpopulation of patients enrolled in the Phase 3 trial. Based strictly on comparison of the mean urine
L2171: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2172: concentrations from uUTI patients to the proposed susceptible breakpoint of 0.5 \mu\text{g/mL}, the Applicant asserts that sulopenem urine concentrations exceed this threshold concentration for at least 80% of the dosing interval. However, no formal target attainment analyses were conducted based on urinary concentrations to support this assertion or illustrate that adequate sulopenem concentrations are achieved at the site of action.
L2173: Is the proposed dosing regimen appropriate for the general patient population for which the indication is being sought?
L2174: The proposed oral dosing regimen for adults is 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil with 500 mg probenecid (one bilayer tablet as a fixed-dose combination) administered twice daily for 5 days for the treatment of uUTI caused by susceptible microorganisms proven or strongly suspected to be non-susceptible to a quinolone. This dosing regimen may not be appropriate because only a subset of the population in the Phase 3 uUTI trial met the predefined margin for demonstration of efficacy relative to ciprofloxacin, which is further corroborated by nonclinical PK/PD findings.
L2175: ## Sulopenem Etzadroxil Dosing
L2176: As with other \beta-lactam antibacterials, the efficacy of sulopenem was expected to be driven by the duration of time that plasma concentrations exceed MIC (i.e., T &gt; \text{MIC}). To support the proposed dosage regimen for the treatment of uUTI, the Applicant conducted PK/PD studies in a murine thigh infection model. These studies were intended to: 1) delineate the relevant PK/PD index for sulopenem, and 2) estimate the magnitude of this index required for various microbiologic endpoints (i.e., bacterial stasis, 1-log, and 2-log CFU/mL reduction in bacterial burden). Per the Applicant's interpretation of the data from these studies, sulopenem's activity was characterized as time dependent. Therefore, a 500 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil in combination with 500 mg probenecid every 12 hours was expected to achieve the T &gt; \text{MIC} target associated with antimicrobial activity over the range of epidemiological \text{MIC}_{90} values observed for target pathogens. However, the Clinical Pharmacology team's assessment of the nonclinical PK/PD studies determined that there was insufficient evidence for the use of T &gt; \text{MIC} as the relevant index for sulopenem. Although not definitive, the overall data trend suggested that sulopenem exhibits concentration-dependent killing against uropathogens (for details, see response to the question regarding clinical pharmacology information to support the proposed breakpoint in this section). If sulopenem's activity is indeed concentration dependent as suggested by these studies, the proposed dosing regimen of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil administered twice daily (in combination with 500 mg probenecid) may be suboptimal. A higher dose of sulopenem etzadroxil would be expected to yield higher urine concentrations of sulopenem and thus be more efficacious for the treatment of uUTI.
L2177: ## Probenecid Dosing
L2178: Because the bilayer tablet includes probenecid, a marketed drug, and the Applicant relied on information described in the FDA-approved labeling for the listed drug, the probenecid
L2179: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2180: component of the formulation was bridged to a commercial probenecid tablet. To this end, the Applicant illustrated that probenecid plasma exposures were comparable following administration of the bilayer tablet and probenecid, USP tablet (an FDA-approved generic drug version of the reference listed drug, Benemid) in Study IT001-105.
L2181: Probenecid lacks antimicrobial activity; instead, it increases plasma exposures of \beta-lactams by decreasing the renal clearance of these drugs. As an adjuvant to \beta-lactam therapy, the recommended daily dose of probenecid is 2000 mg administered in divided doses. For the uUTI drug development program, probenecid dose selection was informed by Studies A8811018 and IT001-101, two Phase 1 studies which evaluated the effect of probenecid doses of 250 mg, 500 mg, and 1000 mg on sulopenem exposure. In Study IT001-101, sulopenem AUCs following administration of sulopenem etzadroxil with either 250 mg or 500 mg probenecid were comparable. In both Studies A8811018 and IT001-101, increasing the dose of probenecid from 500 mg to 1000 mg of probenecid (i.e., a 2-fold increase in dose) resulted in only an additional 1.3 to 1.4-fold increase in sulopenem AUC. The Applicant noted that this additional fold increase in exposure would not result in a clinically relevant increase in T &gt; MIC at MICs of 0.5 \mug/mL and 1 \mug/mL (b) (4)
L2182: Therefore, 500 mg probenecid was expected to be sufficient.
L2183: In Study IT001-102, it was determined that simultaneous administration of a single 500 mg dose of probenecid with sulopenem etzadroxil results in higher plasma sulopenem exposures than either staggering the administration of sulopenem etzadroxil and probenecid, or administering probenecid as 2 divided doses. Based on these findings, 500 mg probenecid was selected for co-formulation with sulopenem etzadroxil.
L2184: When administered as a single 500 mg dose, probenecid increased the plasma AUC of sulopenem by ~1.3 to 1.4-fold compared to administration of 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil alone. Additionally, multiple dose administration of 500 mg probenecid with 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil decreased renal clearance of sulopenem by 1.9-fold and increased sulopenem AUC by 1.8-fold under fed conditions (See Appendix 16.3). The cumulative amount of sulopenem recovered in urine over a 24 h period was comparable in the presence or absence of probenecid. However, because probenecid increases plasma exposures of sulopenem at the expense of diminished renal clearance, its use for the treatment of uUTI may not be appropriate if sulopenem's activity is concentration dependent (as suggested by nonclinical PK/PD studies). Instead, concurrent use of probenecid may promote subtherapeutic urine concentrations of sulopenem and thus contribute to treatment failure.
L2185: ## Sulopenem Etzadroxil With Probenecid Dosing
L2186: The proposed dosing regimen for the treatment of uUTI was evaluated in the Phase 3 uUTI trial, IT001-301, in which adult females with signs and symptoms of uUTI were randomized to receive either 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil with 500 mg probenecid as a fixed-dose combination or ciprofloxacin. The primary study endpoint of overall response (a composite of clinical and microbiological response) was evaluated in 2 separate patient populations: patients who presented with a quinolone-susceptible pathogen at baseline (MMITTS), and patients who
L2187: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2188: presented with a quinolone-resistant pathogen at baseline (MMITTR). In the MMITTR population, sulopenem showed superiority to ciprofloxacin in the treatment of uUTI. However, in the MMITTS population, sulopenem failed to demonstrate noninferiority to ciprofloxacin (See Section 8). Failure to meet the noninferiority margin in the MMITTS population may be indicative of suboptimal dosing of sulopenem etzadroxil as suggested by the nonclinical PK/PD studies. Furthermore, because probenecid may decrease urinary concentrations of sulopenem, its use for a uUTI indication may be inappropriate.
L2189: Is an alternative dosing regimen or management strategy required for subpopulations based on intrinsic patient factors?
L2190: No clinically significant differences in the PK of sulopenem were observed based on age, gender or body weight based on popPK modeling. Hepatic impairment is also not expected to impact the PK of sulopenem. However, use of the sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid fixed-dose combination tablet is not recommended in subjects with CL_{cr} \le 60 mL/min due to safety and efficacy concerns in this subpopulation (as described below).
L2191: ## Hepatic Impairment
L2192: The effect of hepatic impairment on the PK of sulopenem was not studied. In vitro, sulopenem was not metabolized by recombinant CYP or UGT enzymes. Additionally, the mass balance study (Study A8811006) indicated that biliary excretion does not play a role in sulopenem elimination. In the Phase 3 uUTI trial, 20 subjects in the sulopenem arm of the study had a history of liver disease and the incidence of adverse events (AEs) in this subset of subjects (30%) was comparable to that of the general population (25%). In the Phase 3 cUTI trial, 29 subjects with a history of liver disease were identified and in this study, a higher percentage (i.e., 38%) of patients receiving sulopenem experienced adverse events compared to the overall study population (15%). However, given the small number of subjects with hepatic impairment and possible variability in severity of hepatic impairment in the cUTI trial, the safety implications of this difference in the incidence of adverse events are unknown. Based on the totality of available information, hepatic impairment is not expected to significantly impact the PK of sulopenem. Therefore, the proposed dose is expected to be safe in patients with hepatic impairment.
L2193: ## Renal Impairment
L2194: In the mass balance study, following oral administration of a 2000 mg dose of [^{14}C]sulopenem etzadroxil, approximately 26.9% of total radioactivity was recovered in urine as unchanged sulopenem. Based on population PK modeling of data from all Phase 3 trials, a 2-fold increase in AUC was observed with decreasing CL_{cr} following administration of the bilayer tablet. However, multiple confounders may preclude reliable estimation of the effect of renal impairment on sulopenem exposure using population PK modeling (See Appendix 16.3). Ultimately, renal impairment was not associated with an increased incidence of adverse events in the Phase 3 uUTI trial.
L2195: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L2196: In the dedicated renal impairment study (Study A8811009), following administration of a 1000 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil, sulopenem plasma AUC_{0-inf} increased 2.0-, 3.0- and 7.4-fold for subjects with mild, moderate, and severe renal impairment, respectively, compared with subjects with normal renal function. However, these higher exposures were not associated with a higher incidence of TEAEs in subjects with mild, moderate, or severe renal impairment compared to subjects with normal renal function. Notably, PK in patients with CL_{Cr} &lt; 15 mL/min and the effect of dialysis were not assessed in the renal impairment study.
L2197: The renal impairment study did not evaluate the effects of coadministration of probenecid on sulopenem exposure in the various renal function groups. According to the referenced probenecid labeling, the effects of probenecid as an OAT3 inhibitor are diminished in the setting of chronic renal impairment (particularly when estimated glomerular filtration rate is \le 30 mL/min) due to functional decline of tubular secretion. Therefore, coadministration of probenecid is not expected to increase sulopenem exposure to a significant extent in the setting of severe renal impairment and renal failure. The single 1000 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil used in the renal impairment study is expected to be administered as divided doses of 500 mg twice daily for the treatment of uUTI. Because the AUC of sulopenem increased approximately dose proportionally within the sulopenem etzadroxil dose range of 400 to 2000 mg in SAD studies, the estimated sulopenem AUC for a 500 mg dose in subjects with severe renal impairment is approximately 24.0 \mu\text{g}\cdot\text{h}/\text{mL}. This exposure is comparable to that of the MTD (4000 mg) in SAD studies (i.e., 26.9 \mu\text{g}\cdot\text{h}/\text{mL}). The MTD in MAD studies was 1200 mg sulopenem etzadroxil in combination with 1000 mg probenecid BID, which was associated with an AUC of 18.8 \mu\text{g}\cdot\text{h}/\text{mL}. Although this AUC is ~28% lower than the anticipated AUC for a 500 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil in subjects with severe renal impairment, the proposed dose is expected to be safe in subjects with severe renal impairment given sulopenem's short half-life even in the setting of severe renal impairment (i.e., 2.75 h) and the short treatment duration of 5 days.
L2198: As indicated in the FDA guidance on drug development for the treatment of uUTIs, urinary exposures are important for the efficacy of drugs intended for the treatment of uUTI. Subgroup efficacy analyses for the MMITTR population in the Phase 3 uUTI trial showed a lower response rate in subjects with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min in both the sulopenem and ciprofloxacin arms (See Section 8.1.2). The underlying causes of reduced efficacy in subjects with CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min could be multifactorial, with failure to achieve adequate drug exposures in urine as a contributing factor. In the Phase 3 uUTI trial, Day 1 urine concentrations were evaluated in 117 subjects in the sulopenem arm. Of these, only 7 subjects had CL_{Cr} \le 60 mL/min. Study results suggested that compared to subjects with normal renal function, subjects with severe renal impairment (CL_{Cr} &lt; 30 mL/min) exhibited significantly lower sulopenem urine concentrations across the entire 6 h urine collection period as shown in Figure 1. Sulopenem urine concentrations in patients with CL_{Cr} 30 to \le 60 mL/min were also low for the first 2 h collection interval, and increased thereafter.

L2201: Due to the limited number of subjects with urine PK data who had CLr \le 60 mL/min (and especially those with severe renal impairment, where N=1), it is unclear if these observations are representative of the expected difference in sulopenem urine concentrations when compared to subjects with normal renal function. Nonetheless, if the efficacy of sulopenem is concentration dependent, the slower renal clearance (and consequently, lower urine concentrations of sulopenem especially early in the dosing interval) in subjects with moderate and severe impairment may have contributed to the reduced efficacy rate observed in this population.
L2202: Based on the totality of information, the proposed dose is expected to be safe in patients with mild, moderate, or severe renal impairment. Because subjects with CLr &lt; 15 mL/min and subjects on hemodialysis were excluded from the renal impairment study, the safety of sulopenem in this population cannot be ascertained. Additionally, since the drug product is supplied as a fixed-dose combination, dosage reduction (if needed) would not be feasible for such patients. From an efficacy perspective, the proposed dose appears to be less efficacious in subjects with CLr \le 60 mL/min. Furthermore, administration of a higher dose in this population may be infeasible, especially in patients with CLr &lt; 30 mL/min, whose sulopenem plasma exposure following a 500 mg dose of sulopenem etzadroxil is expected to approximate that of the MTD in single and multiple ascending dose studies.
L2203: Because of the above-stated safety and efficacy concerns, administration of the 500 mg sulopenem etzadroxil/500 mg probenecid fixed-dose combination tablet is not recommended in patients with CLr \le 60 mL/min and in patients on hemodialysis.

L2205: Are there clinically relevant food-drug or drug-drug interactions, and what is the appropriate management strategy?
L2206: Yes, food intake increases the bioavailability of sulopenem and may moderately improve the tolerability of sulopenem. Therefore, the sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid bilayer tablet should be administered with food. No clinically relevant drug-drug interactions (DDIs) were observed with sulopenem etzadroxil, sulopenem or probenecid.
