L3409: ## Disk Content Studies
L3410: The Applicant submitted data from disk diffusion susceptibility testing with sulopenem disk masses of 5, 10, and 20 \mug versus broth microdilution MIC testing by using concurrent inoculum of the following pathogens: 110 *S. aureus* (including methicillin-resistant *staphylococcus aureus*), 63 CoNS, 81 *S. pneumoniae*, 26 GAS, 27 GBS, 27 VGS, 105 enterococci, 116 Enterobacteriales (including extended spectrum beta-lactamase), 31 lactose non-fermenting gram-negative bacilli and 91 *H. influenzae* (Study (b) (4) 615). The disk zone diameters and MIC values of the tested isolates were correlated in scatterplots to develop provisional interpretive criteria for the disk diffusion testing of sulopenem. QC ranges have been established using the 2 \mug sulopenem disk.
L3411: ## Correlation of Broth Microdilution vs. Agar Dilution MIC Values
L3412: Susceptibility testing was conducted in parallel by broth microdilution and agar dilution using concurrent inoculum of 398 isolates (106 staphylococci, 102 Enterobacteriales, 102 *S. pneumoniae* and 88 *H. influenzae* isolates) by following the CLSI guidelines (CLSI M07).
L3413: Essential agreement between broth microdilution and agar dilution MIC values did not exceed 95% for any of these tested groups of organisms, however, the maximum agreements of 93.8%, and 94.1% were achieved for methicillin-susceptible *staphylococcus aureus* (n=64) and Enterobacteriales (n=102), respectively.
L3414: ## Quality Control Studies
L3415: Quality control (QC) studies for sulopenem have been conducted using CLSI M23 guidelines for the establishment of QC ranges for broth microdilution susceptibility testing of aerobes (Study (b) (4) 631), and disk diffusion susceptibility testing of Enterobacteriales (Study (b) (4) ITM-004-18).
L3416: ## QC ranges for the Broth Microdilution Testing of Sulopenem Against Aerobes

L3422: ## QC Ranges for the Disk Diffusion Testing of Sulopenem Against Enterobacteriales
L3423: A Tier 2 study was performed to establish the QC range for *E. coli* ATCC 25922 for sulopenem using 2 \mug disks by following the M23 guidelines ((b) (4) ITM-004-18). Two lots of sulopenem 2 \mug disks were used in this study, both manufactured by Liofilchem (Roseto delgli Abruzzi, Italy) and three lots of Mueller-Hinton agar media were used in this study: BBL (Becton-Dickinson, Sparks, MD), Hardy (Santa Maria, CA) and Remel (Lenexa, KS). Eight laboratories participated in the study, and each site tested ten replicates over a three-day period according to the CLSI disk diffusion method (CLSI M02-A13).
L3424: Results were similar by disk lot (mean zones were 26.5 and 26.8 mm) and media (mean zones were 26.3 to 27.0 mm). Disk diffusion susceptibility testing using a disk mass of 2 \mug was selected as the optimum disk mass for the establishment of QC ranges.
L3425: ## 16.5.1.8. Post-Antibiotic Effect
L3426: Post-antibiotic effect (PAE) was observed at 5x and 10x MIC of 0.2 and 0.7 hr for 1 out of 4 *E. coli* isolates tested, specifically ATCC 35218 (TEM-1). PAE was observed at 5x MIC for 0.7 hr for *K. pneumoniae* 396798 (ESBL, CTX-M-15, SHV-1, OXA-1/30) isolate. Sulopenem demonstrated a post-antibiotic sub-inhibitory MIC effect (PAE-SME) of &gt;5 hour at 1/2X MIC for 4 *E. coli* and 2 *K. pneumoniae* isolates. Table 166 summarizes the results.

L3438: ## 16.5.2. Animal Infection Model Studies
L3439: Sulopenem and its oral prodrug sulopenem etzadroxil were evaluated for *in vivo* activity in three animal infection models:
L3440: - The mouse systemic infection model against *S. pneumoniae* and *K. pneumoniae*;
- The mouse pulmonary infection model against *S. pneumoniae*; and
- The Mongolian gerbil otitis media model against *H. influenzae*.
L3441: ## 16.5.2.1. Systemic Infection Models
L3442: Summaries of the in vivo activities of sulopenem and its prodrug, sulopenem etzadroxil dosed orally (PO) or subcutaneously (SC) are presented below:
L3443: **Study RR 810-00093:** Briefly, CF1 mice (n=10) were infected via an intraperitoneal (IP) challenge with 3.5 \times 10^7 CFU/mouse of *K. pneumoniae* 53A1109 isolate. This is an ESBL-producing strain that contains the TEM-1, OXA-9, multiple SHVs and AmpC \beta-lactamase genes with a sulopenem MIC value of 0.25 \mu\text{g/mL}. Compounds in this study were dosed PO or SC at 0.5- and 4.0-hours post-infection to determine the protective dose for 50% of the tested animals (PD50). Sulopenem failed when dosed PO (PD50 &gt;50 mg/kg) but was efficacious when dosed SC, with a PD50 of 3.4 mg/kg, as shown in Table 168. Prodrug sulopenem etzadroxil dosed orally exhibited a PD50 of 9.0 mg/kg in this model.
L3444: **Study RR 810-00093:** CF1 mice (n=10) were infected via an IP challenge with 1.3 \times 10^2 CFU/mouse of *S. pneumoniae* 02J1095. This is a macrolide-resistant, penicillin-tolerant strain with sulopenem MIC value of 0.25 to 0.5 \mu\text{g/mL}. Compounds were administered at 0.5- and 4-hr post-infection. Sulopenem failed when dosed PO (PD50&gt;50 mg/kg) but was efficacious when dosed SC, with a PD50 of 4.3 mg/kg (Table 168). Sulopenem etzadroxil dosed orally exhibited a PD50 of 6.3 mg/kg.
L3445: **Study RR04-25-2006:** CF1 female mice (n=8) were infected via IP injection with 3.5 \times 10^2 CFU/mouse of *S. pneumoniae* 02J1095 strain with sulopenem MIC value of 0.25 to 0.5 \mu\text{g/mL}. Compounds were administered at 0.5- and 4-hr post-infection. When dosed PO, sulopenem failed with a PD50 of &gt;50 mg/kg but was efficacious when dosed SC (PD50 6.3 mg/kg) as shown in Table 168. Sulopenem etzadroxil demonstrated an oral PD50 of 12.5 mg/kg.

L3461: ## 16.5.2.3. Gerbil Otitis Media Models
L3462: The in vivo activity of sulopenem, and the prodrug sulopenem-etzadroxil was investigated in a gerbil model of otitis media caused by *H. influenzae* Rd/AH5-3 strain (\beta-lactamase-negative, ampicillin-resistant with sulopenem MIC value of 0.015 to 0.06 \mu\text{g}/\text{mL}). Briefly, gerbils were infected via direct injection into the middle ear with 1.25 \times 10^7 CFU/gerbil; therapy was initiated 18 hr post-infection and continued three times daily for two days. In this model, sulopenem failed when dosed PO with a PD50 of &gt;50 mg/kg but was efficacious when administered SC with a PD50 of 4.3 mg/kg (Table 170). Sulopenem etzadroxil had an oral PD50 of 4.5 mg/kg.

L3469: ## 16.5.3. Pharmacokinetics/Pharmacodynamics Studies
L3470: (For a detailed review of the PK/PD studies, PTA analysis, and Monte-Carlo simulation, please refer to the Clinical Pharmacology section 6.3.2 of this unireview)
L3471: To evaluate the PK/PD relationship for sulopenem, a mouse thigh infection study was conducted using clinical isolates of *S. pneumoniae*, *S. pyogenes*, *E. coli* and *K. pneumoniae* with different resistant phenotypes. Based on preclinical data, the Applicant states that fT &gt; MIC was the PK/PD target that best correlated with efficacy. However, the FDA Clinical Pharmacology reviewer found significant issues related to the data presented for the PK/PD studies and the data suggest that the PK/PD target index for sulopenem is predicted to be Cmax/MIC based on plasma concentration.
L3472: *Clinical Microbiology Reviewer's Comments: Although the Applicant stated that T &gt; MIC is the PK/PD target for sulopenem that best correlates with efficacy, the FDA Clinical Pharmacology reviewer found significant issues related to the data presented for the PK/PD studies.*
L3473: ## 16.5.4. Clinical Study For Sulopenem: uUTI
L3474: The Applicant conducted a single Phase 3 clinical study (IT001-301) to determine the safety and efficacy of a 5-day course of oral sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid against a 3-day course of oral ciprofloxacin for the treatment of adult female patients (\ge 18 years of age) with uUTI. Additionally, supporting safety data for sulopenem were submitted from two different failed Phase 3 clinical studies conducted for complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI; IT001-302) and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI; IT001-303). The three Phase 3 clinical trials are summarized in Table 171. However, this review focuses primarily on the uUTI trial (IT001-301).
L3475: *Clinical Microbiology Reviewer's Comments: The study results in this section were largely taken from the Applicant's analyses and were used to assist in review of the clinical microbiology data for an initial assessment of possible susceptibility test interpretive criteria/breakpoints. The Clinical Microbiology reviewer defers to the Statistical reviewer for analysis and comment on the Agency's assessment of the efficacy results as noted in Section 8.1 of this unireview.*

L3482: In Study 301, the microbiological modified intent-to-treat (MMITT) population comprised all subjects who had at least one or a maximum of two baseline urinary bacterial pathogen(s) identified from urine with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL. A total of 830 (sulopenem arm, dosed BID for five days) and 829 (ciprofloxacin arm, dosed twice daily for three days) patients were included in the modified intent-to-treat (MITT) population. The primary endpoint for the study was the overall response (clinical and microbiological success) on Day 12 (\pm 1 day) at the test-of-cure (TOC) visit.
L3483: Bacterial urinary pathogens were identified from microbiological culture from acceptable urine specimens collected at baseline, and subsequent visits.
L3484: Among the ITT population, uUTIs were predominantly caused by *E. coli* (56.0% in sulopenem treatment group and 58.4% in ciprofloxacin treatment group), *K. pneumoniae* (6.5% in sulopenem treatment group and 6.0% in ciprofloxacin treatment group), and *P. mirabilis* (2.2% in sulopenem treatment group and 2.1% in ciprofloxacin treatment group).
L3485: ## 16.5.4.1. uUTI Phase 3 Clinical Study, SURE 1: ITO01-301
L3486: ## Methods for Microbiological Collection, Culture, and Identification
L3487: ## Microbiological Sampling
L3488: For microbiological culture and analysis, mid-stream clean-catch urine specimens were collected from patients into a sterile container at Screening (Baseline), Day 3, Day 5 (EOT), Day 12 (TOC), Day 28, and for any study-related visits. All specimens were sent to the local Microbiology laboratory or the regional Microbiology Laboratory (Covance) within 24 hours after collection. In addition, an aliquot of screening/baseline urine samples were also sent to central Microbiology laboratory, International Health Management Associates for the US sites only.
L3489: For the US sites, Covance served as the regional Microbiology Laboratory where isolates were stored in duplicate and where quantitative urine culture, identification and susceptibility testing were performed at all visits. The Central Microbiology Laboratory, IHMA conducted study-specific quantitative urine culture, identification and susceptibility testing/custom MIC and urine Gram stain/reading at Screening/Baseline only. IHMA also stored duplicates of isolates at -80°C and performed re-identification and susceptibility testing of isolates received from Covance.
L3490: For the ex-US sites, [REDACTED] (b) (4) was the Central Laboratory and IHMA was the Central Microbiological Laboratory. [REDACTED] (b) (4) provided study supplies, isolate delivery, and data collection; whereas, IHMA confirmed isolate identification and conducted susceptibility testing and MIC assays, as well as staining and reading the urinary slides prepared at the local laboratories.
L3491: The flowcharts for microbiological procedures in the US sites and ex-US sites are presented in Figure 22.
L3492: **Figure 22. Flow Chart of Microbiology Procedures for the IT001-301 Study: US Sites (Top Figure);
Ex-US Sites (Bottom Figure)**

L3494: ## Organism Isolation And Target uUTI Pathogens
L3495: Urine specimens were plated by calibrated disposable loops (1 \muL and 10 \muL loops) on the following agar plates for colony counts, microbial identification, and susceptibility testing by following standard microbiological procedures:
L3496: - Blood agar plate
- Selective agar for gram-negative rods [e.g., MacConkey or Eosin Methylene Blue plate]
L3497: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L3498: The following organisms were considered as uropathogens when the baseline urine culture grew \ge 10^5 CFU/mL:
L3499: - Enterobacteriales
- *Staphylococcus saprophyticus*
- *Enterococcus* spp.
- *Pseudomonas aeruginosa*
L3500: However, the MMITT population (defined below) for this study only included patients with uUTIs caused by Enterobacteriales and/or *S. saprophyticus* (study uropathogens).
L3501: Microbiological-MITT (or MMITT): MMITT patients were defined as those with a positive study entry urine culture within 48 hours prior to the first dose, with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL of a uropathogen (Enterobacteriales or *Staphylococcus saprophyticus* only) and no more than 2 species of target pathogens identified in the study entry urine culture with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL.
L3502: MMITTS: The MMITTS patients were those MMITT patients with a baseline uropathogen susceptible to the comparator drug, ciprofloxacin (defined as MIC \le 1 mg/L), and no baseline pathogen phenotypically resistant to ciprofloxacin.
L3503: MMITTR: The MMITTR patients were those MMITT patients with a baseline uropathogen resistant to the comparator drug, ciprofloxacin (defined as MIC \ge 2 mg/L).
L3504: ## Microbiological Outcome Measures
L3505: The primary endpoint for the uUTI study was the outcome of Overall Response at the TOC visit which included combined clinical and microbiological responses. However, the microbiological definitions used in the assessment of the per-pathogen microbiological response are summarized in Table 172 and Table 173.
L3506: **Table 172. Baseline Pathogens**
L3507: Response	Definition
Eradication	A urine culture obtained at the timepoint of analysis demonstrated <10^3 CFU/mL of the baseline uropathogen
Persistence	A uropathogen from urine present at baseline regardless of susceptibility grew at \ge 10^3 CFU/mL at the timepoint of analysis*.
Persistence with Increasing MIC	A urine culture taken after at least 2 full days of treatment grew \ge 10^5 CFU/mL of the baseline uropathogen and displayed \ge 4-fold higher MIC to study drug received at the timepoint of analysis.
Indeterminate	Patient was lost to follow-up or an assessment was not undertaken such that no urine culture was obtained (or culture results could not be interpreted) at the timepoint of analysis (contaminated results are considered a negative culture and therefore an eradication6).
L3508: CFU, colony-forming unit; MIC, minimum inhibitory concentration. *The genus/species and susceptibility profiles need to match. Additional molecular testing by pulsed field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) or whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed as needed for confirmation.
L3509: Source: NDA submission
L3510: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L3511: **Table 173. Post-Baseline Pathogens**
L3512: Response	Definition
Superinfection	A uropathogen not present at baseline grew with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL from the first dose of study drug through the EOT visit in the setting of recurrent/persistent/new uUTI symptoms requiring non-study systemic antibacterial treatment* (patient-determined clinical failure at EOT).
New Infection	Isolation of a non-baseline pathogen from a culture post-EOT visit from a urine culture specimen with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL in a patient with one or more new uUTI signs/symptoms requiring new systemic antibacterial treatment* after the EOT visit (patient-determined clinical failure post-EOT).
Recurrence	In a patient with clinical and microbiological success at EOT, isolation of a baseline pathogen from a urine culture specimen with \ge 10^5 CFU/mL post-EOT visit, along with new or recurrence of one or more uUTI signs/symptoms requiring new systemic antibacterial treatment* after the EOT visit (patient-determined clinical failure post-EOT).
Colonization	Isolation of a microorganism from the urine culture after EOT in a patient without one or more signs and symptoms of uUTI and not requiring new systemic antibiotic therapy* (patient-determined clinical success post-EOT).
L3513: * Excluding linezolid, daptomycin, vancomycin, azithromycin, metronidazole, josamycin, macrolide, nifuratel, tergynan, fluconazole, cystone, butoconazole nitrate, clindamycin hydrochloride, clotrimazole, tinidazole and clarithromycin, as well as “antibiotics and chemotherapeutics for dermatological use” and “ophthalmologicals” since they have no activity against the pathogens in the study. CFU, colony-forming unit; EOT, end of treatment; uUTI, uncomplicated urinary tract infection
L3514: Source: NDA submission

L3605: **Clinical Microbiology Reviewer's Comments:** The Agency differed with the Applicant's approach for resolving discordant cipro-susceptibility results and whether or not to assign these subjects to the MMITTR population. The Agency provided guidance that if a subject is found with a cipro-resistant isolate from either a central lab IHMA culture or IHMA confirmatory identification of the local laboratory isolates, then the subject should be included in the MMITTR population. The ciprofloxacin susceptibility should be determined by IHMA based on the MIC broth microdilution assay only. The IHMA in vitro MIC susceptibility results should have priority irrespective of the gyrase PCR results. The Agency found that the proposed PCR for gyrase mutation was not sufficient to determine cipro-susceptibility since other gene mutations may also be involved in determining quinolone-resistance (e.g., *parC*, *parE*) as per current literature. Additionally, the presence of other plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance genes may also confer quinolone resistance.
L3606: ## Summary of Baseline Culture Results: ITT Population
L3607: Approximately 67% of the ITT patients (1072/1590) from both treatment arms had a baseline urine culture with at least one target uropathogen in a quantity of \ge 10^5 CFU/mL, thus qualifying for the MMITT population. The most-frequently isolated uropathogens from urine at concentrations \ge 10^5 CFU/mL in the ITT population are summarized in Table 189. More than half the pathogens isolated were *E. coli* (57.2%; 910/1590); whereas 6.2% were *K. pneumoniae*, 2.1% were *P. mirabilis*, and less than 1% were *S. saprophyticus*.

L3613: ## Efficacy Analysis: Clinical and Microbiological Outcomes

L3615: ## *Correlation of Overall Response and Sulopenem MICs of Key Target Pathogens: MMITT*
L3616: The overall response by target pathogens *E. coli* (N=437), *K. pneumoniae* (N=48) and *P. mirabilis* (N=17) and their MICs for sulopenem in the overall MMITT population are shown in Figure 23, Figure 24, and Figure 25, respectively. Against *E. coli*, the overall rate of success was between 40 and 66.8% across an MIC range of \le 0.015 to 0.25 \mu\text{g/mL}. Against *K. pneumoniae*, an overall success rate of 43 to 100% with an MIC range of \le 0.015 to 8 \mu\text{g/mL}, however, no isolates with an MIC of 0.25 to 2.0 \mu\text{g/mL} were present. Against *P. mirabilis*, success rates were observed between 50 to 100% with an MIC range 0.03 to 0.25 \mu\text{g/mL}.

L3620: ## 16.5.4.2. Emergence of Resistance During Therapy
L3621: ## Impact of Treatment on the Distribution of Susceptibility to the Treatment Regimen
L3622: In this study, no post baseline isolate was observed with a sulopenem MIC that had increased by \ge 4-fold relative to a baseline isolate of the same genus and species. However, there was one patient that was reported to have an MIC increase of \ge 16-fold during therapy. Patient 129-1001 was a 73-year-old woman that had a baseline *E. coli* with an MIC of 0.015 \mu\text{g/mL} and an *E. coli* with an MIC of 0.25 \mu\text{g/mL} was identified at TOC. The baseline isolate with the lowest MIC was compared to the TOC isolate as it was having a \ge 4\times MIC change and was investigated for further analysis. It was revealed that the patient also had an *E. coli* at baseline with the same whole
L3623: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L3624: genome sequence with an MIC of 0.25 \mu\text{g/mL}. All three *E. coli* isolates were susceptible to ertapenem and the patient had fully resolved all uUTI symptoms at the TOC visit. Furthermore, this indicated that a sub-population of the same bacterial species with different MIC values may have been present at baseline.
L3625: Treatment with sulopenem had very little impact on the distribution of MIC's between the pre-treatment and post-treatment isolates. Overall, the MIC50/90 values were 0.03/0.06 \mu\text{g/mL} and 0.03/0.12 \mu\text{g/mL} against pre-treatment and post-treatment isolates, respectively.
L3626: ## Correlation of MIC Values of the Baseline Isolates to Microbiologic Outcome at TOC: MMITT, MMITTS and MMITTR Populations
L3627: The per pathogen microbiologic response of *E. coli*, *K. pneumoniae*, and *P. mirabilis* at TOC by baseline MIC to sulopenem was determined as percent success for the MMITT (overall), the MMITTS and the MMITTR populations. Microbiologic response was defined as microbiologic success at TOC in the microbiologically evaluable (ME-TOC) patients, that is, those that were both clinically and microbiologically evaluable.

No baseline isolates of *K. pneumoniae* were observed that had MIC values between 0.25 to 2 \mu\text{g/mL}, however, two isolates with MIC 4 and 8 \mu\text{g/mL} were observed and this was associated with a favorable outcome.
L3658: ## 16.5.5. Supporting Microbiology Data From Other Phase 3 Studies
L3659: As mentioned earlier, the Applicant conducted two additional Phase 3 studies to evaluate the safety and efficacy of sulopenem for the treatment of cUTI and cIAI indications. Data from both cUTI and cIAI studies were submitted in this NDA application to support the safety of sulopenem administration in uUTI treatment.
L3660: This review only summarizes the microbiological data from cUTI Phase 3 study only (SURE2, IT001-302).
L3661: ## 16.5.5.1. cUTI Phase 3 Study: SURE 2 (Study IT001-302)
L3662: The IV sulopenem alone or followed by PO sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid was compared with IV ertapenem followed by PO ciprofloxacin or amoxicillin-clavulanate in this study for the
L3663: ## NDA Multi-disciplinary Review and Evaluation {NDA 213972}
## {sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid}
L3664: treatment of adult patients with cUTI at the TOC visit (Day 21\pm1 day). A total of 1356 patients were randomized (1:1 fashion) in this study.
L3665: ## Microbiological Sampling, Culture and Pathogen Identification: cUTI
L3666: Urine specimens were collected for culture at Screening (Baseline), Day 5, Day 10 (\pm1 day; EOT), Day 21 (\pm1 day; TOC), and any study-related visits by following standard procedures. Additionally, two sets of blood culture bottles were to be collected aseptically at each visit (one aerobic and one anaerobic) by following a standard procedure. According to the Applicant, (b) (4) was the Central Laboratory and IHMA was the Central Microbiological Laboratory in both the US and in Europe. Routine culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (except study drug) was to be performed at the local laboratories against all gram-negative pathogens. The Central Microbiology Laboratory, IHMA, only received all isolates from the local laboratories and confirmed the identification with further analysis. These procedures are outlined in the following Figure 33.

L3735: ## Correlation of microbiological success to MIC values of baseline *E. coli*, *K. pneumoniae*, and *P. mirabilis* isolates
L3736: In the uUTI clinical study, the microbiological success in relation to MIC values of baseline *E. coli*, *K. pneumoniae*, and *P. mirabilis* isolates from the sulopenem treatment group the in MMITT (MMITTR and MMITTS) population at the TOC visit are summarized below:
L3737: - Among 437 baseline *E. coli* isolates with an MIC range of 0.015 to 1.0 µg/mL, the overall microbiological eradication rate at TOC was 76.4%. The highest sulopenem MIC that correspond to microbiological success was 0.25 µg/mL and 3/5 (60%) isolates were eradicated. Only one baseline *E. coli* isolate with a sulopenem MIC of 1 µg/mL was available but persisted. No baseline isolate with MIC values at ≥2 µg/mL was available. The MIC50/90 was 0.03/0.06 µg/mL against all *E. coli* isolates from both surveillance and clinical studies. Therefore, a susceptible BP of 0.25 µg/mL would be reasonable and will cover most *E. coli* population.
- Among 48 baseline *K. pneumoniae* isolates with an MIC range 0.015 to 8.0 µg/mL, the overall microbiological eradication rate at TOC was 77.1%. The highest sulopenem MIC that correspond to favorable microbiological eradication was 0.12 µg/mL and 7/8 (87.5%) isolates at this MIC were successfully eradicated. No baseline isolate was available with MIC values between 0.25 to 2.0 µg/mL. However, only 2 baseline isolates with MIC values 4 and 8 µg/mL were available but eradicated. The MIC50/90 was 0.03/0.12 against all *K. pneumoniae* isolates from both surveillance (US and Europe) and clinical studies. Therefore, a susceptible BP of 0.25 µg/mL would also be reasonable and would cover most *K. pneumoniae*.
- Among 17 baseline *P. mirabilis* isolates with an MIC range of 0.03 to 0.25 µg/mL, the overall microbiological eradication rate at TOC was 82.4%. The highest sulopenem MIC that correspond to microbiological success was 0.25 µg/mL and 10/10 (100%) isolates at this MIC were successfully eradicated. No baseline isolate was available at MIC values ≥0.5 µg/mL. Against *P. mirabilis* isolates from both surveillance and clinical studies, the MIC50/90 was between 0.12/0.25 to 0.25/0.5 µg/mL. Therefore, a susceptible BP of 0.25 µg/mL would also be reasonable and would cover most *P. mirabilis*.
L3738: In summary, the overall microbiological success was observed in patients with baseline isolates of *E. coli* and *P. mirabilis* that had MIC values of ≤0.015 to 0.25 µg/mL. No baseline *E. coli* isolate at MIC 0.5 µg/mL was available but a single isolate at MIC 1.0 µg/mL was available with microbiologic failure. No baseline *P. mirabilis* isolate with MIC ≥0.5 µg/mL was available. The overall microbiological success was observed in patients with baseline *K. pneumoniae* isolates that had MIC values of ≤0.015 up to 0.12 µg/mL. No baseline *K. pneumoniae* isolates with MIC values between 0.25 to 2 µg/mL were available, however, only two isolates at MIC 4 and 8 µg/mL were available with overall success outcome.
L3739: Therefore, the Clinical Microbiology team recommends revised sulopenem S/I/R MIC BPs of ≤0.25/0.5/≥1.0 µg/mL against Enterobacteriales (*E. coli*, *K. pneumoniae*, and *P. mirabilis* only). The corresponding disk diffusion zone diameter BPs have been calculated by following CLSI

L3803: Diagram illustrating the Population Pharmacokinetic (PopPK) model structure. The model consists of a Central Compartment (V1) and two Peripheral Compartments (V2 and V3). The Central Compartment is connected to V2 via exchange rates K_{12} and K_{21}, and to V3 via exchange rates K_{13} and K_{31}.
Drug administration occurs via two routes:
Route 1 (sulopenem): Sulopenem is administered intravenously (IV) and undergoes absorption from the Central Compartment (abs_{1,1}) to abs_{2,1} (absorption rate constant K_{a1}). The absorption rate constant is defined as K_a = (N_r + 1)/M_{rr}.
Route 2 (sulopenem etzadroxil): Sulopenem etzadroxil is administered orally (FR1) and undergoes absorption from the Central Compartment (abs_{2,1}) to abs_{2,2} (absorption rate constant K_{a2}). The fraction of drug absorbed is defined as FR_2 = (1 - FR_1).
The model also includes a term T_{M}^*C_s/(K_{M}^* + C_s) associated with the Central Compartment, likely representing a mechanism of action or target-mediated drug disposition.

The q1h voiding interval generally shows higher PTA values across the MIC range compared to the q2h voiding interval, and the Fed condition generally shows slightly higher PTA values compared to the Fasted condition.

L3829: Figure 9: Scheme of Model Structure of the Final PopPK Model. The diagram illustrates a pharmacokinetic model with two parallel absorption chains leading to a central compartment (V1) and two peripheral compartments (V2 and V3). Sulopenem etzadroxil is absorbed via two routes: FR1 leading to abs_1,1 and FR2=(1-FR1) leading to abs_2,1. These absorption compartments transition through transit compartments (abs_1,NTR1 and abs_2,NTR2) with transit rates Ktr1 and Ktr2, respectively, before entering the Central Compartment (V1). The Central Compartment (V1) receives input from the absorption chains and is connected to Peripheral Compartment 2 (V2) via intercompartment clearance Q1 (K12 and K21) and Peripheral Compartment 3 (V3) via intercompartment clearance Q2 (K13 and K31). The Central Compartment (V1) also shows elimination (Ku = (Ntr+1)/Mtr) and a saturable elimination pathway (TM*Cs/(KM+Cs)). Sulopenem is shown as an external input.
